candidates: When building a URL string for insertion into an unquoted CSS `url()` function (e.g., for SVG marker references), use `CSS.escape()` rather than manually replacing individual characters such as `\(`, `\)`, or `\\`. Manual replacement is incomplete: characters that are valid in URIs but invalid in CSS `<url-token>` values — including single quotes, double quotes, and whitespace — will still cause breakage. The shared `getUrl()` helper in `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/common/common.ts` centralises this logic and should be reused instead of inlining the pattern.

In changeset files, use `patch` for bug fixes, `minor` for additive features, and `major` only for breaking changes that require a major version bump. Using `major` for a non-breaking fix forces an unnecessary major release; verify the bump type matches the nature of the change before merging.

Changeset description messages should precisely identify the condition under which the bug manifests (e.g., which config option must be enabled) and describe what the fix actually resolves. Avoid vague or security-adjacent language (e.g., 'unsafe') when the real impact is functional correctness. A good description tells future readers when to expect the bug and what changed to fix it.
